## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

15	### 2.1 什么是有序回归
16	
17	想象预测水泥的强度等级：1 级最弱，5 级最强。这些标签有三个特点：
18	
19	- **有序**：3 级比 2 级强，「差一档」是一个真实的概念；
20	- **间距未知**：2 级与 3 级的强度差，未必等于 3 级与 4 级的强度差；
21	- **类别数有限**：不是任意实数。
22	
23	这类问题既不是标准分类，也不是标准回归：
24	
25	| 路线 | 隐含假设 | 用在有序标签上的毛病 |
26	| --- | --- | --- |
27	| 多分类（softmax + CE） | 类别之间毫无关系 | 把「预测 2 级真实 3 级」与「预测 5 级真实 3 级」视为同等错误，顺序信息完全浪费 |
28	| 回归（MSE） | 标签是等距数值 | 强行假设「档距相等」，且预测可能落在 2.7 这类无意义的档位上 |
29	| **有序回归** | 有序、间距未知 | 在两者之间建模——正是本讲主题 |
30

35	CORAL 与 CORN 共享同一个出发点，叫**扩展二元分类（extended binary classification）**：把 \(K\) 类有序问题改写成 \(K-1\) 个二元问题——
36	
37	\[
38	\text{任务 } k:\quad \text{「标签 } y \text{ 是否大于 } k \text{？」}\qquad k = 0, 1, \dots, K-2
39	\]
40	
41	以 \(K=5\) 为例，一个真实标签 \(y=3\) 的样本，其扩展二元标签是：
42	
43	\[
44	[\,y>0,\; y>1,\; y>2,\; y>3\,] = [1, 1, 1, 0]
45	\]
46

170	### 4.2 CORAL 层与损失：共享权重 + 独立偏置
171	
172	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
173	
174	CORAL（**CO**nstant **R**ank-consistent **A**pproach to ordinal regression **L**ayers，Cao, Mirjalili & Raschka 2020）把扩展二元分类落到实处：\(K-1\) 个二元任务的 logit 定义为
175	
176	\[
177	\text{logit}_k(x) = f(x) + b_k,\qquad k=0,\dots,K-2
178	\]
179	
180	其中 \(f(x)\) 是**共享的**单输出线性打分 \(w^\top h(x)\)（\(h(x)\) 是倒数第二隐藏层输出），\(b_k\) 是**各自独立**的偏置。对每个任务单独做二元交叉熵，加起来就是 CORAL 损失：
181	
182	\[
183	\mathcal{L}_{\text{CORAL}} = -\sum_{k=0}^{K-2}\Big[\, \mathbb{1}[y>k]\log\sigma(f(x)+b_k) + \mathbb{1}[y\le k]\log\big(1-\sigma(f(x)+b_k)\big) \Big]
184	\]
185	
186	它的妙处在**秩一致性（rank consistency）是结构白送的**。注意每个任务输出的累积概率：
187	
188	\[
189	P(y>k\mid x) = \sigma\big(f(x)+b_k\big)
190	\]
191	
192	sigmoid 单调，所以只要偏置有序 \(b_0 \ge b_1 \ge \dots \ge b_{K-2}\)，就有 \(P(y>0\mid x)\ge P(y>1\mid x)\ge\dots\)——而「标签越大、超过它的概率越小」正是有序数据的基本公理。CORAL 论文证明：共享权重的结构让偏置在训练中保持这一顺序。对比之下，若给每个任务配独立权重（老方法 Niu et al. 2016 的做法），每个二元分类器各学各的，完全可能学出 \(P(y>0|x) < P(y>1|x)\) 这种自相矛盾的概率。
193	
194	预测时从累积概率回收标签。因为 \(y>k\) 对 \(k=0,\dots,y-1\) 全真、对 \(k\ge y\) 全假，最自然的规则是**数一数有多少个任务认为「超过」**：把 \(\sigma(\text{logit}_k)>0.5\) 的任务个数作为预测档位。4.2.4 的实践就是亲手实现这个转换。
195	
196	与基线相比，改动的只有输出层与损失：softmax 消失了，取而代之的是 \(K-1\) 个独立的 sigmoid。

282	**练习 1**：`CoralLayer` 的参数量随类别数 \(K\) 怎么增长？和基线的 `Linear(300, K)` 比呢？

284	**答案**：`coral_weights` 是 `Linear(size_in, 1, bias=False)`，参数 \(= \text{size\_in}\)；偏置是 \(K-1\) 维。总共 \(\text{size\_in} + K - 1\)，即 300 维隐藏层、5 类时仅 304 个参数；基线 `Linear(300, 5)` 是 \(300\times5+5=1505\) 个。类别越多差距越大——共享权重把「每个类一套权重」压缩成「全体类一套打分器 + 每类一个门槛」。

292	**答案**：仍不报错——输出头变成 19 个 logit，`levels` 变 19 维，其中任务 5~18 的目标恒 0；浪费参数与算力，且损失被一堆「学永假」的任务稀释。评估端 `proba_to_label` 对 19 维累积概率数票，预测档位仍只会在 0~4 出现（因为任务 5 以后永远投不出「超过」票——除非训练不充分），MAE 大体仍可计算。这说明扩展二元框架对「类别数写大」是静默容忍的，比 CE 的显式报错更隐蔽。
293	
294	### 4.3 CORN 条件概率：链式法则分解
295	
296	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
297	
298	CORN（**CO**nditional **R**ank-consistent **N**eural network，Shi, Cao & Raschka 2021）对同一串二元任务换了一种提问方式。CORAL 的任务 \(k\) 直接问无条件问题「\(P(y>k)\)」；CORN 改问**条件**问题：
299	
300	\[
301	\text{任务 } k:\quad P\big(y > k \,\big|\, y > k-1\big)
302	\]
303	
304	即「已知标签超过了 \(k-1\)，它也超过 \(k\) 的概率是多少？」。链式法则（概率乘法法则）把条件概率串回无条件的累积概率：
305	
306	\[
307	P(y>k\mid x) = \prod_{j=0}^{k} P\big(y>j\,\big|\,y>j-1,\,x\big),\qquad \text{约定 } P(y>0\mid y>-1)=P(y>0)
308	\]
309	
310	这正是 notebook 结尾那句「sigmoid 得条件概率、链式法则得任务概率」的数学含义。好处有两层：
311	
312	1. **无需共享权重**。每个任务一个独立的 logit（普通 `Linear` 输出 \(K-1\) 维即可），表达能力比 CORAL 的单标量打分更强；秩一致性由 `cumprod`（连乘非负概率）自动成立——乘出来的序列天然非递增。
313	2. **损失只算「有定义」的任务**。对真实标签 \(y\) 的样本：任务 \(0..y-1\) 的事件确定为真（目标 1）、任务 \(y\) 的事件确定为假（目标 0）、而任务 \(y+1..K-2\) 的**条件**（\(y>y\)）已知不成立，条件概率无定义，**不参与损失**。这份「相关性掩码」由 `corn_loss` 内部处理，调用者无感。
314	
315	对比一句话记牢：**CORAL 用结构（共享打分器）换秩一致，CORN 用条件化（乘积链）换秩一致**；两者都不需要 softmax，都在 \(K-1\) 个二元任务上训练，最后都把累积概率换算回档位。
316	
317	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
318	
319	```text
320	隐藏层输出 ──Linear(→K-1)──▶ logits（每维 = 一个条件任务的 logit）
321	                                    │
322	        整数标签 y ──corn_loss(logits, y, K)──▶ 掩码 BCE：任务 0..y 目标 1/0，
323	                                    │          任务 y+1 之后不参与损失
324	                                    ▼
325	                            五步训练循环（不变）
326	                                    │
327	评估/秩概率：logits ──sigmoid──▶ 条件概率 P(y>k|y>k-1)
328	                        ──cumprod(dim=1)──▶ 累积概率 P(y>0), P(y>1), ...
329	                        ──(>0.5 计数)──▶ 预测档位 ──▶ MAE
330	```
331	
332	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
333	
334	设置与模型——改动比 CORAL 还小：
335

360	#### 4.3.4 代码实践
361	
362	**实践目标**：不借助 `corn_label_from_logits`，用 `sigmoid` + `cumprod` + 自写计数规则，手工复现 CORN 的预测，并与官方函数对账。

369	# 示例代码：手工还原 CORN 的 秩概率 → 档位

393	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
394	
395	**练习 1**：CORAL 与 CORN 的输出层宽度都是 \(K-1\)，但参数量差多少？各自为什么？
396	
397	**答案**：CORN 的 `Linear(300, 4)` 有 \(300\times4+4=1204\) 个参数；CORAL 是共享打分器 \(300\) 加 4 个偏置共 304 个，约为 CORN 的 1/4。CORAL 用一个标量打分强制所有任务共享「强度方向」，只允许门槛不同；CORN 给每个任务独立打分的自由度。约束强未必差——样本少时 CORAL 的强先验反而抗过拟合。
398	
399	**练习 2**：CORN 损失里「任务 \(y+1\) 之后不参与损失」为什么是必要的，而不是偷懒？

401	**答案**：任务 \(k>y\) 建模的是 \(P(y>k \mid y>k-1)\)，而该样本已知 \(y>k-1\) 为假——条件事件不发生，条件概率在该样本上无观测意义，任何目标值都编不出来。硬给它一个目标（比如 0）等于逼模型学「在永远不会出现的条件分支上的行为」，会污染梯度。掩码掉是数学上的必然。

403	**练习 3**：三个 notebook 的初始训练损失分别是 1.85（CE）、7.88（CORAL）、44.56（CORN）。能据此说 CORN「学得最差」吗？

426	
427	## 6. 本讲小结
428	
429	- **有序回归**处理「有序但间距未知」的标签；CE 分类器把错 1 档与错 4 档同罚，训练目标与 MAE 评估标准错位，这是它作为有序基线的结构性缺陷。
430	- **扩展二元分类**把 \(K\) 类有序问题改写成 \(K-1\) 个「标签是否超过 \(k\)」的二元任务，顺序信息编码在扩展标签（如 \(y=3 \to [1,1,1,0]\)）里。
431	- **CORAL** = 共享权重单打分器 + \(K-1\) 个独立偏置（递减初始化），logit \(=f(x)+b_k\)；sigmoid 单调性 + 偏置有序让累积概率天然非递增，秩一致性由结构保证；预测 = 数「\(\sigma>0.5\)」的任务数。
432	- **CORN** = 普通 `Linear(→K-1)` 输出条件概率 \(P(y>k\mid y>k-1)\)，`cumprod` 链式法则还原累积概率；条件不成立的任务被掩码在损失之外；秩一致性由概率连乘保证。

436	## 7. 下一步学习建议
437	
438	- **横向扩展方法**：`pytorch_ipynb/ordinal/` 目录还有三份姊妹 notebook——`beckham2016_cement.ipynb`（不可逆有序损失）、`niu2016_cement.ipynb`（多输出独立二元分类器，正好是 CORAL 所批评的无共享结构）、`polat2022_cement.ipynb`（自蒸馏式有序回归）。带着本讲的框架去读：各自的输出层是什么、秩一致性靠什么保证，你会读得非常快。
439	- **读论文原文**：CORAL（Pattern Recognition Letters 140, 325-331, 2020）与 CORN（arXiv:2111.08851），重点看 CORAL 关于偏置有序性的证明与 CORN 的消融实验。
440	- **应用到你自己的数据**：任何「评分/等级/组别」型任务（满意度调查、信用分级、年龄组）都适用；沿用第 5 节的受控实验模板，把 CE 基线与 CORAL/CORN 各跑一遍。
441	- **手册内衔接**：下一讲 u7-l6 进入模型可解释性可视化（显著性图与 guided backprop），从「怎么评估模型的错」转向「怎么看模型在看哪里」；若想先补评估方法论的另一半，可回顾 u7-l2 的 K 折交叉验证——本讲 998 样本的小数据场景正是 K 折的主场。

# 有序回归：CORAL 与 CORN

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清**有序回归（ordinal regression）**是什么问题：标签有先后顺序、但相邻标签之间的「距离」未知，它夹在普通分类与普通回归之间。
2. 理解把交叉熵（CE）分类器直接用在有序标签上的缺陷：它把「错 1 档」与「错 4 档」当成同等的错误。
3. 掌握 **CORAL** 的核心设计——共享权重 + 独立偏置的输出层：输出 \(K-1\) 个二元任务，靠结构（而不是损失惩罚）保证秩一致性。
4. 掌握 **CORN** 的另一条路线——条件概率 + 链式法则分解：输出层退回普通 `Linear`，秩概率用 `cumprod` 还原。
5. 会把累积概率转换回最终的有序类别预测，并用 MAE/MSE 评估有序模型——这是本讲代码实践的核心任务。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 什么是有序回归

想象预测水泥的强度等级：1 级最弱，5 级最强。这些标签有三个特点：

- **有序**：3 级比 2 级强，「差一档」是一个真实的概念；
- **间距未知**：2 级与 3 级的强度差，未必等于 3 级与 4 级的强度差；
- **类别数有限**：不是任意实数。

这类问题既不是标准分类，也不是标准回归：

| 路线 | 隐含假设 | 用在有序标签上的毛病 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 多分类（softmax + CE） | 类别之间毫无关系 | 把「预测 2 级真实 3 级」与「预测 5 级真实 3 级」视为同等错误，顺序信息完全浪费 |
| 回归（MSE） | 标签是等距数值 | 强行假设「档距相等」，且预测可能落在 2.7 这类无意义的档位上 |
| **有序回归** | 有序、间距未知 | 在两者之间建模——正是本讲主题 |

类似的问题到处都是：电影评分（1~5 星）、年龄组估计、疼痛等级、信用评级。u2-l2 讲的 MNIST 恰恰**不是**有序数据（数字 1 和 2 的图像之间没有「大小」关系），这也是本讲换用水泥强度数据集的原因。

### 2.2 关键直觉：把有序问题拆成一串二元问题

CORAL 与 CORN 共享同一个出发点，叫**扩展二元分类（extended binary classification）**：把 \(K\) 类有序问题改写成 \(K-1\) 个二元问题——

\[
\text{任务 } k:\quad \text{「标签 } y \text{ 是否大于 } k \text{？」}\qquad k = 0, 1, \dots, K-2
\]

以 \(K=5\) 为例，一个真实标签 \(y=3\) 的样本，其扩展二元标签是：

\[
[\,y>0,\; y>1,\; y>2,\; y>3\,] = [1, 1, 1, 0]
\]

顺序信息就藏在这串编码里：标签越大，前面连续的 1 越多。两个方法分道扬镳的地方在于——**这 \(K-1\) 个二元任务的输出头怎么设计、损失怎么算**：

- **CORAL**：所有任务共享同一个权重向量，只有偏置不同（秩一致性靠结构保证）；
- **CORN**：各任务独立输出，但建模的是**条件**概率，用链式法则还原（秩一致性靠概率乘积保证）。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 有序回归问题定义与 CE 基线

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

基线模型是我们最熟悉的普通多分类器：MLP 最后一层输出 5 个 logits，用 softmax + 交叉熵训练，预测时取 `argmax`。它完全不感知标签的顺序。

为什么它是有序任务的「不合格」基线？交叉熵只要求**正确类的概率最大**。对一个真实标签为 3 的样本，把概率质量挪给 2 类还是挪给 0 类，损失下降一样多——梯度不区分「近错」与「远错」。评估时我们却用 MAE（平均绝对误差）打分，MAE 明确认为错 1 档比错 4 档好。**训练目标与评估标准错位**，就是 CE 基线的结构性缺陷，也正是 CORAL/CORN 要修复的东西。

顺带认识数据集：水泥强度（cement_strength）数据，998 个样本、8 个连续特征（V1~V8，成分配比）、5 个有序强度等级。原始标签是 1~5，代码统一减 1 变成 0~4（PyTorch 的损失函数要求标签从 0 开始编号）。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么评估用 MAE 而不用准确率？CE 分类器的准确率能达到很高，说明什么？

**答案**：MAE 把「错 1 档」计 1 分、「错 3 档」计 3 分，度量的是错误的**Ordinal 距离**；准确率只看对错，0/1 计分，错 1 档和错 4 档同罚。对有序任务，两个准确率相同的模型，MAE 可以差很远——MAE 才与「强度估计得准不准」的业务含义对齐。

**练习 2**：把本 notebook 的 `NUM_CLASSES` 改成 4 会发生什么？

**答案**：`cross_entropy` 会直接报错（标签 4 越界：合法标签是 0~3）。`NUM_CLASSES` 决定输出层宽度与合法标签范围，必须与数据实际档数一致；这个「必须相等」的约束在 4.2 会被 CORAL 的一个真实笔误打破，值得记住。

**练习 3**：`MyDataset` 里为什么特征要 `astype(np.float32)`，而标签不用转？

**答案**：PyTorch 的默认张量类型是 `float32`，`nn.Linear` 等层的权重也是 `float32`，特征不转会在 `model(features)` 处报 dtype 不匹配（`float64` vs `float32`）。标签交给 `cross_entropy` 时要求整数类型，numpy 的 int 数组经 collate 自动变成 `int64` 张量，刚好合规。

### 4.2 CORAL 层与损失：共享权重 + 独立偏置

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

CORAL（**CO**nstant **R**ank-consistent **A**pproach to ordinal regression **L**ayers，Cao, Mirjalili & Raschka 2020）把扩展二元分类落到实处：\(K-1\) 个二元任务的 logit 定义为

\[
\text{logit}_k(x) = f(x) + b_k,\qquad k=0,\dots,K-2
\]

其中 \(f(x)\) 是**共享的**单输出线性打分 \(w^\top h(x)\)（\(h(x)\) 是倒数第二隐藏层输出），\(b_k\) 是**各自独立**的偏置。对每个任务单独做二元交叉熵，加起来就是 CORAL 损失：

\[
\mathcal{L}_{\text{CORAL}} = -\sum_{k=0}^{K-2}\Big[\, \mathbb{1}[y>k]\log\sigma(f(x)+b_k) + \mathbb{1}[y\le k]\log\big(1-\sigma(f(x)+b_k)\big) \Big]
\]

它的妙处在**秩一致性（rank consistency）是结构白送的**。注意每个任务输出的累积概率：

\[
P(y>k\mid x) = \sigma\big(f(x)+b_k\big)
\]

sigmoid 单调，所以只要偏置有序 \(b_0 \ge b_1 \ge \dots \ge b_{K-2}\)，就有 \(P(y>0\mid x)\ge P(y>1\mid x)\ge\dots\)——而「标签越大、超过它的概率越小」正是有序数据的基本公理。CORAL 论文证明：共享权重的结构让偏置在训练中保持这一顺序。对比之下，若给每个任务配独立权重（老方法 Niu et al. 2016 的做法），每个二元分类器各学各的，完全可能学出 \(P(y>0|x) < P(y>1|x)\) 这种自相矛盾的概率。

预测时从累积概率回收标签。因为 \(y>k\) 对 \(k=0,\dots,y-1\) 全真、对 \(k\ge y\) 全假，最自然的规则是**数一数有多少个任务认为「超过」**：把 \(\sigma(\text{logit}_k)>0.5\) 的任务个数作为预测档位。4.2.4 的实践就是亲手实现这个转换。

与基线相比，改动的只有输出层与损失：softmax 消失了，取而代之的是 \(K-1\) 个独立的 sigmoid。

**练习 1**：`CoralLayer` 的参数量随类别数 \(K\) 怎么增长？和基线的 `Linear(300, K)` 比呢？

**答案**：`coral_weights` 是 `Linear(size_in, 1, bias=False)`，参数 \(= \text{size\_in}\)；偏置是 \(K-1\) 维。总共 \(\text{size\_in} + K - 1\)，即 300 维隐藏层、5 类时仅 304 个参数；基线 `Linear(300, 5)` 是 \(300\times5+5=1505\) 个。类别越多差距越大——共享权重把「每个类一套权重」压缩成「全体类一套打分器 + 每类一个门槛」。

**练习 2**：为什么偏置预初始化用**递减**序列而不是全零？全零会怎样？

**答案**：全零初始化时所有任务起点相同（\(P(y>k)=\sigma(f(x))\) 全相等），任务间没有先验的次序梯度，早期训练里「永真任务」（小 k）与「永假任务」（大 k）要自己把偏置拉开，收敛更慢。递减初始化让一开始就有 \(b_0>b_1>\dots\)，配合 docstring 所说学习更快、泛化更好。注意秩一致性本身由共享权重结构保证，初始化只是给了一个好的起点。

**练习 3**：本 notebook 的 `NUM_CLASSES=10` 若改成 20，训练与评估会分别发生什么？

**答案**：仍不报错——输出头变成 19 个 logit，`levels` 变 19 维，其中任务 5~18 的目标恒 0；浪费参数与算力，且损失被一堆「学永假」的任务稀释。评估端 `proba_to_label` 对 19 维累积概率数票，预测档位仍只会在 0~4 出现（因为任务 5 以后永远投不出「超过」票——除非训练不充分），MAE 大体仍可计算。这说明扩展二元框架对「类别数写大」是静默容忍的，比 CE 的显式报错更隐蔽。

### 4.3 CORN 条件概率：链式法则分解

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

CORN（**CO**nditional **R**ank-consistent **N**eural network，Shi, Cao & Raschka 2021）对同一串二元任务换了一种提问方式。CORAL 的任务 \(k\) 直接问无条件问题「\(P(y>k)\)」；CORN 改问**条件**问题：

\[
\text{任务 } k:\quad P\big(y > k \,\big|\, y > k-1\big)
\]

即「已知标签超过了 \(k-1\)，它也超过 \(k\) 的概率是多少？」。链式法则（概率乘法法则）把条件概率串回无条件的累积概率：

\[
P(y>k\mid x) = \prod_{j=0}^{k} P\big(y>j\,\big|\,y>j-1,\,x\big),\qquad \text{约定 } P(y>0\mid y>-1)=P(y>0)
\]

这正是 notebook 结尾那句「sigmoid 得条件概率、链式法则得任务概率」的数学含义。好处有两层：

1. **无需共享权重**。每个任务一个独立的 logit（普通 `Linear` 输出 \(K-1\) 维即可），表达能力比 CORAL 的单标量打分更强；秩一致性由 `cumprod`（连乘非负概率）自动成立——乘出来的序列天然非递增。
2. **损失只算「有定义」的任务**。对真实标签 \(y\) 的样本：任务 \(0..y-1\) 的事件确定为真（目标 1）、任务 \(y\) 的事件确定为假（目标 0）、而任务 \(y+1..K-2\) 的**条件**（\(y>y\)）已知不成立，条件概率无定义，**不参与损失**。这份「相关性掩码」由 `corn_loss` 内部处理，调用者无感。

对比一句话记牢：**CORAL 用结构（共享打分器）换秩一致，CORN 用条件化（乘积链）换秩一致**；两者都不需要 softmax，都在 \(K-1\) 个二元任务上训练，最后都把累积概率换算回档位。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
隐藏层输出 ──Linear(→K-1)──▶ logits（每维 = 一个条件任务的 logit）
                                    │
        整数标签 y ──corn_loss(logits, y, K)──▶ 掩码 BCE：任务 0..y 目标 1/0，
                                    │          任务 y+1 之后不参与损失
                                    ▼
                            五步训练循环（不变）
                                    │
评估/秩概率：logits ──sigmoid──▶ 条件概率 P(y>k|y>k-1)
                        ──cumprod(dim=1)──▶ 累积概率 P(y>0), P(y>1), ...
                        ──(>0.5 计数)──▶ 预测档位 ──▶ MAE
```

from coral_pytorch.dataset import corn_label_from_logits

    cond = torch.sigmoid(logits)        # 条件概率 P(y>k | y>k-1)
    cum = torch.cumprod(cond, dim=1)    # 链式法则 → 累积概率 P(y>k)

    print(torch.equal(mine, official), (mine - official).abs().sum().item())
    cond = torch.sigmoid(logits)
    print((torch.cumprod(cond, dim=1)[:, :-1] >= torch.cumprod(cond, dim=1)[:, 1:]).all())

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：CORAL 与 CORN 的输出层宽度都是 \(K-1\)，但参数量差多少？各自为什么？

**答案**：CORN 的 `Linear(300, 4)` 有 \(300\times4+4=1204\) 个参数；CORAL 是共享打分器 \(300\) 加 4 个偏置共 304 个，约为 CORN 的 1/4。CORAL 用一个标量打分强制所有任务共享「强度方向」，只允许门槛不同；CORN 给每个任务独立打分的自由度。约束强未必差——样本少时 CORAL 的强先验反而抗过拟合。

**练习 2**：CORN 损失里「任务 \(y+1\) 之后不参与损失」为什么是必要的，而不是偷懒？

**答案**：任务 \(k>y\) 建模的是 \(P(y>k \mid y>k-1)\)，而该样本已知 \(y>k-1\) 为假——条件事件不发生，条件概率在该样本上无观测意义，任何目标值都编不出来。硬给它一个目标（比如 0）等于逼模型学「在永远不会出现的条件分支上的行为」，会污染梯度。掩码掉是数学上的必然。

**练习 3**：三个 notebook 的初始训练损失分别是 1.85（CE）、7.88（CORAL）、44.56（CORN）。能据此说 CORN「学得最差」吗？

## 6. 本讲小结

- **有序回归**处理「有序但间距未知」的标签；CE 分类器把错 1 档与错 4 档同罚，训练目标与 MAE 评估标准错位，这是它作为有序基线的结构性缺陷。
- **扩展二元分类**把 \(K\) 类有序问题改写成 \(K-1\) 个「标签是否超过 \(k\)」的二元任务，顺序信息编码在扩展标签（如 \(y=3 \to [1,1,1,0]\)）里。

- **CORN** = 普通 `Linear(→K-1)` 输出条件概率 \(P(y>k\mid y>k-1)\)，`cumprod` 链式法则还原累积概率；条件不成立的任务被掩码在损失之外；秩一致性由概率连乘保证。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
